messages.subject: Re: Plot format
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zhou,

Unfortunately, it supports only pdf files. (because separate pages for each protein are needed.) However, I believe that pdf can be changed to any other format easily with some application or software, such as adobe acrobat and so on.

Hope to be helpful.

-Meena

messages.subject: Multimarker model using MS stat
messages.body_plain:
I am working on a project that aims to detect multimarker model for breast cancer progression prediction.
I have the Ms data and trying to build the multimarker model and I wonder if MS stat have the code that can build this model from our data.
Our data composed of markers intensities in both cases and control and we are planning to build a model which is made of the best combined markers that have the highest  sensitivity and specificity rate.
We've already built the pairwise model using logisitc regression where we judge the robustness of the paired marker based on the ROC curve they produce compared to their single ROC.
Now we are planning to try every single possible combination and evaluate the effect of adding a marker on the ROC.

For example:
If a marker A has an AUC(Area under the curve of 0.7), then adding marker B improved the AUC to 0.78. Adding marker C to the already combined (A+B) reduces the AUC to 0.7, than we should not consider marker C in this combination and we can move to evaluate adding marker D to ( A+B) and so on . We consider the markers that when combined, the AUC of the combined markers is improving.

Any suggestions?

messages.subject: Re: Multimarker model using MS stat
messages.body_plain:
Dear Adhari,

MSstats is only designed for class comparison (i.e., testing), and not for class prediction (i.e., supervised classification such as logistic regression). However, you can use the 'subject quantification' part of the workflow, to obtain one number per protein per subject. These can be used as inputs to logistic regression, or to any other classification model.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat
Sincerely
Olga

messages.subject: Problem instaling MSstats on MAC OS
messages.subject_clean: Problem instaling MSstats on MAC OS
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys

I would like to use MSstats on my MAC and as far as I understand, Skyline is only available for Windows. So I would have to use MSstats as a R package. Is that correct?

My version of R is 3.2.0 and I am running MAC OS 10.7.5 which is a bit out of date. I hope this is not a problem.

I tried to install MSstats following the commands given in the installation page:

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("MSstats")
library(MSstats)

but it installs an old version of the package that does not have some functions that I need, such as plotProfiles. Then I moved to the second option which is download the new version MSstats.daily_3.0.1.tar.gz and follow the RScript also available in the website. However, I got this error message:

install.packages(pkgs="~/Desktop/MSstats.daily_3.0.1.tar.gz",repos=NULL,type="source")

Error in rawToChar(block[seq_len(ns)]) :

Warning in install.packages :
 installation of package ‘/Users/barbarahenning/Desktop/MSstats.daily_3.0.1.tar.gz’ had non-zero exit status

Do you guys have any idea of what could be wrong?

Thanks in advance.
Matheus Viana
University of California Irvine
